text:
maia: heads-up — ran into a flakey RuntimeError when the python SDK AsyncClient is created at module import time in our ASGI app. app crashes on first request in dev but only sometimes in CI. :confused:

devon: ugh can you paste the trace? sounds like the usual "no running loop" stuff from creating async objects in sync context.

maia: stack: `RuntimeError: no running event loop` followed by a long httpx/aiohttp init stack. minimal repro below:

```python
# main.py (sync import at module level)
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)  # created during import

def create_app():
    from fastapi import FastAPI
    app = FastAPI()
    @app.get('/')
    async def root():
        return await client.generate('hi')
    return app

# uvicorn main:create_app --reload
```

maia: When uvicorn reloads we sometimes get `RuntimeError: asyncio.get_event_loop() is deprecated` or "no running event loop". Happens more in pytest with any tests that import main.py (so creating client outside startup).

alex: yep that's the pattern — constructing an AsyncClient at import time can bind internal transport/session to the current loop (or try to grab one). In processes where there is no running loop yet you get those errors. Also triggers unclosed tasks warnings on shutdown.

sam: short-term fix: move client creation to async startup handler or use a sync factory that defers async init. Example:

```python
# app lifecycle pattern
client = None

async def startup():
    global client
    client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)

async def shutdown():
    await client.aclose()

app.add_event_handler('startup', startup)
app.add_event_handler('shutdown', shutdown)
```

devon: thanks, can you open an issue with a repro + note that the SDK should avoid doing background async work in __init__? If constructing transport/session is costly we should provide an explicit sync-safe constructor or a factory `from_sync()` that doesn't touch the loop.

maia: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/issues/412 with repro and CI logs. added labels: "bug", "sdk-python", "needs-triage". pinging @devon to own triage. :eyes:

ci-bot: Issue created by maia: #412 — "AsyncClient: import-time init causing event loop errors / unclosed tasks" — linked PR suggestions welcome.

devon: will take a look tomorrow. potential fixes: document pattern + add runtime guard that defers creating loop-bound objects until `await client._ensure_initialized()` or provide a synchronous mode that uses blocking HTTP fallback. Also add a unit test that imports module in pure-sync test runner to catch regressions.

maia: sounds good. also adding a quick note to the onboarding docs warning against top-level AsyncClient creation.

alex: :thumbsup: if you want I can draft a small PR that adds an async init + raises a helpful error when created in sync context.

maia: please do — thanks!
